title: Residential Electricity Supply Customer Agreement: Change-in-Law Pass-Through
content:
**Section 1.** A fixed or time-of-use rate on a Residential Electricity Supply agreement may change during the term only to pass through a change in law or regulation, and only on a plan that permits regulatory pass-through.

**Section 2.** A regulatory pass-through notice must be issued at least the plan's minimum regulatory-change notice period, in calendar days, before its effective date. The new rate applies to cycles beginning on or after the later of the stated effective date and the notice date plus that notice period.

**Section 3.** On a plan that does not permit regulatory pass-through, the contract rate is guaranteed for the whole term, and any pass-through billed on it is a billing error to be corrected under the billing correction rules.

**Section 4.** A regulatory pass-through is not a ground for waiving the early termination fee.

## Applying Section 2 (hypothetical dates, with the 30-day notice period every plan carries)

| Notice date | Stated effective date | Notice date plus 30 days | The later of the two | New rate reaches cycles beginning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| March 1 | April 15 | March 31 | April 15 | on or after April 15 |
| March 20 | April 1 | April 19 | April 19 | on or after April 19 |
| March 2 | April 1 | April 1 | April 1 | on or after April 1 |

## Applying Section 3

A pass-through rate billed during the term on Beacon Ridge Price Lock 24, Beacon Ridge Clean Wind 24 or Beacon Ridge Monthly Variable (plans that do not permit regulatory pass-through) is a billing error. A customer who ends a fixed term because a pass-through raised the rate is not relieved of the early termination fee on that ground.
